title: Substitution
examples: Can you show me how to substitute a negative number into an expression?
If I use a formula, do I use the variable name or the number value?
What happens when I substitute a value for a variable with a power?

explain.say: Today we are learning about substitution in algebra. Substitution means replacing a letter with a number. You will use the given values to find the answer.
First, we must remember the rules for negatives and powers. A negative number raised to an even power is always positive. For example, negative two squared is positive four.
Next, we look at substituting values into a formula. You must replace every instance of the variable with the given number. Remember to use brackets when substituting.

Let us try an example. If y equals three x plus two, and x equals negative one. You substitute negative one for x. So y equals three times negative one plus two. This gives y equals negative three plus two, which is negative one.

faq.q: What is the difference between using parentheses and not using them?
faq.a: Parentheses are very important when substituting values. They help you keep track of negative signs and the order of operations. You should always use them when replacing a variable.
asks: Do I always use brackets when substituting?
Why do I need parentheses here?

faq.q: How do I handle a negative number raised to an odd power?
faq.a: If a negative number is raised to an odd power, the result will be negative. For example, negative three cubed is negative twenty-seven. The sign stays negative.
asks: Is negative to the power of three negative?
What is the sign rule for odd powers?

faq.q: If the formula has multiple variables, do I substitute them one by one?
faq.a: Yes, you substitute every variable with its given value. You must do this for every single letter in the formula. Work carefully to keep track of each replacement.
asks: Do I substitute all variables at once?
What if there are two variables in the formula?

faq.q: What if the variable is in the denominator of a fraction?
faq.a: You treat the whole fraction as one expression. You must substitute the value into every spot. Remember that division is the same as dividing by. Be careful with negative signs in the denominator.
asks: How do I substitute in a fraction?
Does the denominator change the process?

faq.q: Can I substitute zero for a variable?
faq.a: Yes, you can substitute zero for any variable. This will usually make the calculation much simpler. All terms containing that variable will become zero.

facts: Negative numbers raised to an even power result in a positive number.
When substituting, always use brackets around the value you replace the variable with.
The order of operations, or BODMAS, still applies after substitution.
A variable represents a value that can change in an equation.

quiz.say: Evaluate the expression 5 times (x - 2) when x equals negative 3.
quiz.why: You substitute negative three for x, making it five times (negative three minus two). This equals five times negative five, which is negative twenty-five.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you calculate 5 times (-3) minus 2, forgetting to put the subtraction inside the brackets first.
wrong.1: This mistake occurs if you calculate five times (negative three plus two), incorrectly changing the subtraction sign.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you forget the negative sign and calculate five times (three minus two).

quiz.say: Find the value of y in the formula y = 2x² + 1 when x equals negative 4.
quiz.why: You substitute negative four for x, giving two times (negative four squared) plus one. Negative four squared is sixteen, so two times sixteen plus one equals thirty-three. Wait, two times sixteen is thirty-two, plus one is thirty-three. Let me recheck my math. Two times sixteen is thirty-two. Thirty-two plus one is thirty-three. Let's recheck the correct answer. Ah, I see the error in the question setup. Let's assume the correct answer is 33.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you forget to square the negative sign and calculate two times negative four plus one.
wrong.2: This mistake occurs if you only substitute the value into the 'plus one' part and ignore the x squared term.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you calculate two times (negative four) plus one, ignoring the power entirely.

quiz.say: What is the value of a in the formula a = (x + 5) / 2 when x equals 1?
quiz.why: You substitute one for x, giving (one plus five) divided by two. This equals six divided by two, which is three.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you only calculate the top part, (x plus 5), and forget to divide by two.
wrong.2: This mistake occurs if you substitute one for x and then only take the value of the numerator.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you incorrectly divide only the 'x' by two, leaving the five alone.
